alternatives.why_less_likely: While payments slowed, the dominant observable failures were gateway timeouts to orders and order queue buildup, which are better explained by orders capacity saturation.

causal_chain.claim: Orders had all workers busy and queue depth increased, indicating capacity saturation.
Gateway calls to orders timed out without receiving a response.
Gateway returned error responses (504 upstream_timeout or 500 internal_error) to entry requests.

root_cause.summary: Orders exhausted its worker capacity, causing requests to queue and gateway calls to time out.

verification.reason: no replayable condition matches this hypothesis

alternatives.why_less_likely: Orders' slowdown appears to be a consequence of payments saturation and retry amplification; there is no evidence of an independent orders processing regression (no deploy/config change).

causal_chain.claim: Payments workers saturated and queue building, leading to load shedding.
Orders began timing out on calls to payments due to payments' slowness.
Orders started receiving 503 errors from payments as payments overloaded and shed load.
Orders became overloaded (queue full, high latency) due to payments failures and retries.
Gateway began timing out on calls to orders due to orders' slowness.
Gateway became overloaded and returned 5xx errors and high latency.

root_cause.summary: Payments became overloaded, causing request queue buildup, increased latency, and load shedding, which triggered timeouts and retries in upstream services.
